accepted_decisions.operative_body: That Council Approve the City of Langford disbursements from January 2021, as outlined in the Accounts Payable Report dated February 04, 2021.

That Council Approve the following funding applications, or deny due to budgetary constraints, for the year 2021: 1. Historically Funded Requests: a) Vancouver Island South Film and Media Commission - $5,000 to promote the industry; b) Greater Victoria Bike to Work Society - $1,500 to offer two bike skills programs to Langford youth; c) Royal Canadian Legion - $3,000 for Remembrance Day luncheon; plus, funding of $3,000 towards a Christmas Dinner 2021; d) Goldstream Nature House - Chums sponsorship program $1,000; e) Big Brothers Big Sisters of Victoria and Area - $2,000 for mentoring program f) Open Gate Church $4,000 to provide fresh produce to needy individuals and families in the Westshore; g) Victoria Sexual Assault Centre $5,000 contribution towards maintaining the Sexual Assault clinic which supports Langford residents; and h) Victoria Women's Transition House Society -funding of $3,000 for support of the Victoria Women's Transition House Violence is Preventable Program. 2. New Requests: j) Fed Urban Agriculture Society - $1,000 for garden kits for those disproportionately affected by pandemic. Provide education on food awareness and food security; and k) Juan de Fuca Senior Citizens Association - $3,000 towards the installation of two hands-free door openers for two of the six washrooms in the Juan de Fuca 55+ Activity Centre. That Council deny the following requests: i) Wild Wise no amount indicated, donation for education on coexisting with wild animals.

That Development Variance Permit No. DVP20-0007 be issued by the Council for the City of Langford to Matt Pike of On Point Engineering Ltd. has applied on behalf of Westhills Land Corp. for a Development Variance Permit to reduce the required amount of off-street parking for an apartment development comprised of two buildings with a cumulative total of 127 units at 3003 Irwin Road subject to the following terms and conditions: 1. Appendix The site shall be developed in accordance with the site plan attached (Appendix A) to the Planning, Zoning and Affordable Housing report dated 20210111. 2. Variances The following regulations of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 are varied under Section 498 of the Local Government Act: a) That Section 4.01.01 of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied to reduce the off-street parking for a two- building, 127-unit development from the required 1.5 parking spaces per dwelling unit plus 1 per 4 dwelling units assigned to visitors to 1.25 parking space per dwelling unit containing 2 bedrooms or less, of which 0.10 is assigned to visitors; 3. Conditions The following requirements are imposed under Section 498 of the Local Government Act: a) That a minimum of five additional street parking spaces be created adjacent to the project; b) That a minimum of 1 parking space is allocated to each residential unit; c) That a minimum of 13 parking spaces are allocated for the exclusive use of visitors to subject apartment building; d) That, prior to issuance of a Building Permit, a Section 219 Covenant is registered in priority of all other charges on title that agrees that the minimum number of parking stalls specified in conditions (ii) and (iii) above are allocated accordingly; and that these parking spaces are not separated from individual units nor provided in exchange for compensation separate than that of a residential unit.

accepted_decisions.operative_body: That Development Variance Permit No. DVP20-0013 be issued by the Council for the City of Langford to Ron Coutre on behalf of Ryan Craycroft to vary the requirements of the RR5 Zone such that lots less than 40 ha may be created by subdivision when not connected to the municipal sanitary sewer system, and to vary the requirements of Development and Servicing Bylaw No. 1000 such that only one emergency access route is provided within 305 m of the development site, for portions of the properties at 738 and 742 Walfred Road, subject to the following terms and conditions: 1. Variances a) That Section 6.14.02(2) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied such that lots less than 40 ha may be created by subdivision when not connected to the municipal sanitary sewer system; b) That section 4.17.1 of Zoning Bylaw No. 1000 be varied such that only one emergency access route is provided within 305 m of the development site; 2. Conditions The following requirements are imposed under Section 498 of the Local Government Act: a) That the proposed pedestrian trail north of the subject property is constructed on the adjacent parcel, connecting the site to lower Walfred Road, prior to occupancy permit of the subject properties; b) That the applicant retains a registered professional forester to develop a wildfire protection plan based on Firesmart principles for the subdivision, including fuel mitigation in the three priority zones (0-10m, 10-30m and 30m+) on the subject properties; and c) That funding for the pedestrian pathway, including a detailed cost estimate, has been confirmed by the City of Langford, prior to DVP issuance.

That Development Variance Permit No. DVP20-0014 be issued by the Council for the City of Langford to Ryan Mogensen of Ecoasis Development LLP on behalf of BM Highlander Development Ltd for a development variance permit to reduce the required amount of off-street parking for a 209-unit apartment at 1995 and 2000 Hannington subject to the following terms and conditions: 1. Conditions The following requirements are imposed under Section 498 of the Local Government Act: a) That a minimum of 1 parking space is allocated to each residential unit; b) That a minimum of 18 parking spaces are allocated for the exclusive use of visitors to subject apartment building; and c) That, prior to issuance of a Building Permit, a Section 219 Covenant is registered in priority of all other charges on title that agrees that the minimum number of parking stalls specified in conditions (i) and (ii) above are allocated accordingly; and that these parking spaces are not separated from individual units nor provided in exchange for compensation separate than that of a residential unit.

accepted_decisions.operative_body: That Council pass the following motion: BE IT RESOLVED that pursuant to section 18 of the Expropriation Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 125, the Council of the Corporation of the City of Langford, as the approving authority for the expropriation completed in the expropriation notice dated December 2, 2020, and filed in the Victoria Land Title Office under number CA8650385 and the expropriation notice dated December 2, 2020, and registered in the Victoria Land Title Office under number CA8650386 (collectively, the ''Expropriation Notices'') does: (a) Acknowledge that it has been served with the Expropriation Notices and a copy of the Expropriation Act; AND (b) Approve the expropriations contemplated by the Expropriation Notices. BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the Corporate Officer is authorized and directed to: (a) Sign the Certificate of Approval in the form prescribed under the Expropriation Act General Regulation; (b) Notify or cause to be notified the expropriating authority and each Owner (as defined in the Expropriation Act) of the Council's approval of the expropriations; (c) Make the advance payments as required under section 20(1)(d) of the Expropriation Act and serve the Notices of Advance Payment in the form prescribed under the Expropriation Act General Regulation with a copy of all appraisal and other reports on which the advance payment is based; (d) File or cause to be filed in the Land Title Office Vesting Notices under section 23 of the Expropriation Act in the form prescribed under the Expropriation Act General Regulation and then serve a copy of the Vesting Notices on each owner (as defined in the Expropriation Act); AND (e) Sign the Notices of Advance Payment and the Vesting Notices.
